summary.locked_approach: Row-level and resample each image to square pixels, then use targeted Fourier reflection mapping to detect and characterize the mica atomic lattice periodicity/order and compare how lattice spacing, coherence, and ordered-domain fraction change from 2 mM to 10 mM KCl.

detailed_analysis:
Two AFM height maps of the same mica/KCl system were analyzed at 2 mM and 10 mM KCl using two independent, methodologically distinct pipelines (both quality-approved, scores 0.86 and 0.93). The central objective—characterizing how surface structure/adsorbate order changes between 2 mM and 10 mM KCl—cannot be answered affirmatively at the level of confirmed atomic lattice: BOTH concentrations, in BOTH pipelines, return domain_confirmed=False and no_resolvable_lattice. The most robust and honest finding of this series is a negative one: no ordered atomic lattice or ordered adsorbate superstructure clears the significance/domain-confirmation gate at either concentration.

What structure IS detected is only tentative. Pipeline 1 (dual-frame FFT) reports a marginal reflection at ~0.485 nm (sigma 7.63) for the 2 mM frame but explicitly labels it 'unconfirmed_tentative_reflection' because the domain-vs-bulk spot SNR ratio (1.57x) falls well below the 3.0x acceptance threshold. Pipeline 2 (per-frame calibrated), which restricts the search to the mica atomic band (0.4-0.6 nm) using each frame's own metadata-derived pixel size, finds a candidate near 0.537 nm (2 mM, sigma 0.68) and 0.501 nm (10 mM, sigma 1.76)—both far below the 3-sigma null. The two pipelines disagree on the exact candidate spacing and on which frame shows the stronger reflection, which is itself diagnostic: a genuine, robust lattice would be reproduced across pipelines. The lack of cross-pipeline reproducibility reinforces the 'no confirmed lattice' verdict.

A critical, well-documented complication is z-calibration. The 2 mM frame metadata reports a data range of 0-1210.7 nm, which would imply an Rq of ~116 nm—physically impossible for atomically flat mica (ceiling ~100 pm). Pipeline 2 correctly flags this z-calibration as 'suspect' and withholds a physical Rq. The 10 mM frame, with a plausible 6 pm data span, yields a physically reasonable Rq of ~0.67 pm. Consequently, the two frames' roughness values are NOT directly comparable, and Pipeline 1's apparent 'Rq decrease' from ~53864 pm to ~0.49 pm is an artifact of inconsistent z-unit handling (nm vs pm) rather than a real roughening/smoothing transition. The pixel-size calibration also differs between frames (~0.059 vs ~0.086 nm/px in Pipeline 2) because the two images have genuinely different fields of view (15.03 vs 22.04 nm), which the more rigorous Pipeline 2 handled with per-frame metadata.

A residual vertical FFT streak (fast-scan-axis line noise) is documented as a physical instrumental limitation that persists after 2nd-order per-row detrending; this depresses achievable spot SNR and is a plausible contributor to the failure to confirm any lattice. In summary, within the limits of these two images, there is no statistically defensible evidence for a KCl-concentration-driven change in ordered surface structure; both surfaces are best described as disordered / lacking a resolvable atomic lattice at the imposed confidence gate.

scientific_claims.claim: Neither the 2 mM nor the 10 mM KCl mica surface exhibits a statistically confirmed atomic lattice or ordered adsorbate superstructure; both frames, across two independent analysis pipelines, fail the domain-vs-bulk SNR (>=3.0x) and 3-sigma significance gates, so no KCl-concentration-dependent change in surface ordering can be substantiated from these data.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Establishes an honest, gated negative result that prevents over-interpretation of marginal FFT reflections as ion-induced ordering, and sets a quantitative confidence bar (SNR ratio, sigma) for future higher-quality acquisitions aiming to detect epitaxial ion adsorption layers on mica.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone demonstrated, with domain-confirmed and cross-pipeline-reproducible FFT lattice detection, that increasing KCl concentration from 2 to 10 mM induces or suppresses an ordered adsorbate lattice on mica in solution?

scientific_claims.claim: The 2 mM frame carries a physically implausible z-calibration (implied data range 0-1210.7 nm -> Rq ~116 nm >> flat-mica ceiling ~100 pm), rendering cross-concentration roughness (Rq) comparison uncomputable; only the 10 mM frame yields a physical Rq (~0.67 pm).
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Demonstrates that apparent roughness 'trends' between the two frames are calibration artifacts, not physics, and underscores the necessity of per-frame z-unit validation before any quantitative morphology comparison in solution AFM.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone quantified how inconsistent z-unit metadata (nm vs pm) can masquerade as concentration-dependent roughness changes in liquid-cell AFM of mica?

individual_results.name: (hard) fmica 2mM KCl
individual_results.analysis_type: Dual-frame (2 mM & 10 mM) pipeline with EXPLICIT multi-file loading (STEP 0): per-image z-calibration (nm) -> per-row polynomial leveling (2nd-order FFT input, 1st-order Rq) -> per-frame square-pixel resample -> fourier_reflection_map lattice detection, gated on explicit domain_confirmed + spot_snr ratio

individual_results.name: (hard) fmica 10mM KCl
individual_results.analysis_type: Per-frame per-row leveling -> PER-FRAME pixel size from EACH frame's OWN metadata/FOV (resolve_pixel_size_nm, distinct meta_2mM/meta_10mM variables + hard assert the nm/px differ) -> z-unit reconciliation to common pm with a flat-mica plausibility gate -> square-pixel resample -> targeted fourier_reflection_map restricted to the mica atomic band (0.4-0.6 nm) with EACH frame's OWN pixel size, honestly gated on the tool's own significance/domain-confirmation fields, + physically-gated Rq (pm); identical pipeline on BOTH frames with a 2 mM vs 10 mM cross-concentration comparison.

flagged_images_analysis.summary: Formally, zero images were flagged by the series QC layer (both approved). However, the trend dashboard marks every per-frame data point with a red X because each frame carries at least one disqualifying quality condition: unconfirmed/absent lattice (domain_confirmed=False, no_resolvable_lattice=True) in all frames, plus a suspect z-calibration in the 2 mM frame. These are honesty/confidence flags, not analysis failures.
possible_causes: Genuinely disordered surface or mobile/loosely-bound ion adsorbate that does not form a static resolvable lattice under the imaging conditions
Insufficient spatial resolution / tip convolution obscuring a sub-nm atomic lattice
Residual fast-scan-axis line noise (documented FFT vertical streak) depressing spot SNR below the acceptance threshold
Corrupt or mislabeled z-unit metadata for the 2 mM frame (0-1210.7 nm range implies impossible ~116 nm roughness on atomically flat mica)
Thermal drift or piezo creep during liquid-cell imaging degrading lattice coherence
recommended_followup: Re-acquire both frames with slower scan rates and drift correction to raise achievable spot SNR above 3.0x
Verify and correct the 2 mM z-calibration (confirm whether the 0-1210.7 nm range is a unit-label error, e.g., should be pm)
Acquire multiple frames per concentration to enable statistical (n>=3) domain-fraction and Rq comparisons rather than n=1 per condition
Perform lattice-resolution imaging with a sharper/characterized tip and, if possible, on a freshly cleaved reference region to confirm the mica lattice is detectable by the pipeline at all
flagged_images_analysis.scientific_significance: The flags represent methodological confidence limits rather than novel physics. The consistent inability to confirm a lattice at either concentration is itself an informative (negative) result, but the flags caution strongly against interpreting the marginal reflections or the Rq difference as real concentration-dependent effects.

refit_analysis.summary: No image was adaptively re-analyzed within a single pipeline; rather, the series was deliberately processed by two parallel, independent pipelines to test reproducibility. This is a cross-pipeline robustness design, not a triggered refit.

pipeline_changes.from_pipeline: Pipeline 1: dual-frame FFT with per-image z-calibration, per-row polynomial (2nd-order) leveling, fallback FOV-derived pixel size, and domain/SNR-gated lattice detection
pipeline_changes.to_pipeline: Pipeline 2: per-frame pixel size from each frame's OWN metadata/FOV (asserted distinct), z-unit reconciliation to common pm with a flat-mica plausibility gate, and lattice search restricted to the 0.4-0.6 nm mica atomic band
pipeline_changes.interpretation: The two pipelines differ chiefly in calibration rigor: Pipeline 2 correctly derived distinct per-frame pixel sizes from the differing FOVs and explicitly caught the 2 mM z-calibration as physically implausible, whereas Pipeline 1 used a fallback pixel size and produced a nm/pm-inconsistent Rq comparison. The concordant conclusion (no confirmed lattice) despite different candidate spacings validates the negative result.

refit_analysis.scientific_implications: The cross-pipeline agreement on the qualitative verdict (no domain-confirmed lattice at either concentration) strengthens confidence that this is a real property of the data, not a single-pipeline artifact. The disagreement on the exact tentative spacing and on Rq behavior localizes the uncertainty to calibration and marginal-signal regimes, pinpointing z-unit metadata integrity and line-noise suppression as the key experimental improvements needed before any KCl-concentration structural claim could be made.

trend_analysis.approach: Single control variable (KCl concentration: 2 vs 10 mM) with TWO independent analysis pipelines (results index 0 and 1) that both report per-frame features. I plot each key feature as a function of KCl concentration (x-axis), overlaying both pipelines as distinct series so the reader can judge reproducibility/robustness of each claimed trend. Because both frames report domain_confirmed=False and no_resolvable_lattice, the dashboard emphasizes the HONEST verdict: no confirmed lattice change, and the Rq comparison is calibration-limited (2 mM z-cal SUSPECT in pipeline 1). I annotate calibration-invalid points rather than drawing misleading regression lines through them. Regression lines are only drawn where >=3 physically-valid points of the same metric exist; with just two concentrations per pipeline I instead draw connecting trend segments and clearly label them as 2-point guides, avoiding overclaiming a quantitative model from n=2.
trend_analysis.flagged_handling: No images were flagged in the series. The script still contains logic to overlay red X markers on any point whose frame reports a disqualifying quality flag (z_calibration_plausibility_flag=='suspect', Rq_is_physical False, domain_confirmed False, or no_resolvable_lattice) so calibration/confidence problems are visually distinguished from clean measurements.

lattice_spacing_nm.interpretation: Only tentative candidate reflections in the 0.48-0.54 nm mica band; none domain-confirmed, and pipelines disagree on the exact value, so no meaningful concentration-dependent spacing change can be claimed.

reflection_coherence_sigma.interpretation: Pipeline 2 shows a modest sigma increase (0.68->1.76) from 2 to 10 mM, but both remain far below the 3-sigma null; Pipeline 1 shows the opposite ordering. Not a reliable trend.

spot_snr_ratio_domain_bulk.interpretation: All values fall under (Pipeline 1) or only marginally near (Pipeline 2) the 3.0x acceptance threshold, confirming no ordered domain stands out from bulk at either concentration.

ordered_domain_fraction.interpretation: Reported as 0 or null in all frames; consistent with a disordered or non-lattice-resolved surface.

Rq_roughness.interpretation: 2 mM Rq is calibration-invalid (z-cal suspect); only 10 mM (~0.67 pm) is physical. Any apparent decrease is an artifact of nm/pm z-unit inconsistency, not real morphology.

pixel_size_nm.interpretation: Larger pixel size at 10 mM (~0.086 nm/px vs ~0.059 nm/px) simply reflects the larger field of view (22.04 vs 15.03 nm); it is an acquisition setting, not a physical property of the surface.

caveats: Only n=1 image per concentration limits any comparison to two data points, precluding statistical regression and making distinction between concentration effects and frame-to-frame variability impossible. The two frames were acquired at different fields of view (15.03 vs 22.04 nm), so pixel size and spatial-frequency sampling differ between conditions, complicating direct FFT comparison. The 2 mM frame's z-calibration is documented as suspect (implies impossible ~116 nm roughness), so its roughness/Rq is not physical and cross-concentration Rq deltas are withheld. A residual fast-scan-axis FFT streak is a documented instrumental limitation that suppresses spot SNR and may itself prevent detection of a real lattice. All lattice 'candidates' are below the significance/domain-confirmation thresholds and are inconsistent between pipelines; they should NOT be interpreted as measured lattice constants. The overarching objective—how structure changes between 2 and 10 mM KCl—remains unresolved: the data support only a gated negative conclusion (no confirmed ordered structure at either concentration), not a positive characterization of a concentration-driven structural transition.

locked_analysis_config.analysis_approach: Row-level and resample each image to square pixels, then use targeted Fourier reflection mapping to detect and characterize the mica atomic lattice periodicity/order and compare how lattice spacing, coherence, and ordered-domain fraction change from 2 mM to 10 mM KCl.
locked_analysis_config.processing_pipeline: Per-row median subtraction for line-by-line leveling (documented; features occupy a fraction of each line so median is robust) -> resample to square physical pixels using metadata FOV (record nm/px via resolve_pixel_size_nm) -> fourier_reflection_map(pixel_size_nm) to detect lattice reflections and map the strongest/ordered reflection (amplitude, domain_mask, domain_fraction, spot_snr_domain vs spot_snr_bulk) -> report lattice spacing (nm), reflection sigma, and ordered-domain fraction; if no reflection clears the floor report 'no resolvable lattice / disordered adsorbate'.
features_to_extract: surface roughness Rq (in physical height units, pm/nm)
locked_analysis_config.quality_criteria: Preprocessing: horizontal striping visibly removed after row leveling; resampled 10 mM image has square pixels with recorded nm/px matching FOV/N to floating-point tolerance; height values reported in physical units (nm or pm), not dtype counts. Science: for 2 mM, a lattice reflection is detected with sigma above the tool's floor and spacing physically plausible for mica (roughly 0.4-0.6 nm); domain map is spatially coherent (not pure noise). For 10 mM, the tool may correctly report no resolvable lattice (disordered adsorbate) or a weaker/less-coherent reflection — either is an acceptable, physically meaningful outcome. Accept/reject on the tool's own significance and spot_snr fields, not a self-imposed numeric threshold.
